claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be prepared as a uniform single-phase high-temperature BCC state by rapid quenching.
Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 has a critical annealing regime approximately between 900 °C and 1100 °C in which an ordered secondary phase forms.
Al has an ordering tendency that can affect the stability of ordered phases in multicomponent Fe-Cr-Ni-based alloys.
Al preferential ordering lowers the free-energy barrier for ordered-phase nucleation in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The ordered secondary phase produced in the proposed regime is likely B2.
The ordered phase nucleates and grows within a metastable BCC matrix.
At high temperatures, Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 retains a metastable BCC state.
Annealing temperature and thermal history can alter phase constitution and precipitation behavior in multicomponent alloys.
Diffusion in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is sufficiently active between 900 °C and 1100 °C, given adequate dwell time, to enable ordered-phase nucleation and growth.
Al-induced thermodynamic instability and temperature-dependent diffusion jointly govern phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Samples annealed inside the proposed window for sufficient dwell times will develop diffraction peaks or microstructural markers characteristic of an ordered phase such as B2.
Samples annealed outside the 900–1100 °C regime will remain predominantly BCC.
Above 1100 °C, the thermodynamic driving force for ordering is insufficient.
Below 900 °C, diffusion is too slow for the transformation to occur within practical experimental timescales.
Local-composition variations and minor inhomogeneities may shift the transformation temperature limits and required dwell times.
